timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed full projected source entry. This is transport-only CLI stream data; semantic events are represented in actor trajectories.
Reviewed main parent trajectory. It performs setup, launches workflow, continues implementation, verifies tests, and handles closure.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the six compatibility library task: API constants, moves importer, iterator/dict helpers, byte/string utilities, metaclass tools, unittest helpers, docs, packaging, and official tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent handled implementation and delivery, then delegated broad audit dimensions to workflow children while continuing local fixes and verification.
parallel.implementation: Copied upstream six 1.17.0 sources, created packaging/support files, removed tests_require, added test_six.py and pre-commit config, then added a raw_input moved attribute.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent integrated all changes in the shared /workspace and artifact validation captured the workspace; child auditors did not own final assembly.
parallel.verification: Parent ran full pytest after raw_input for 201 passed; workflow children ran additional install, API, moves, packaging, and critic audits with mixed minor findings.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The agent process was killed at the time limit and some audit tail state remained, but official evaluation completed ok true and no unmet task requirement is evidenced.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same six compatibility and packaging requirements from the identical prompt, including pip install, test suite, and supporting files.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor performed all exploration, implementation, verification, and final reporting; serial protocol validation shows no delegation.
serial.implementation: Wrote six.py, compared it to upstream six 1.17.0, aligned it byte-for-byte, and produced setup/config/docs/support files.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Assembled the final 13-file tree locally, cleaned transient artifacts, and ended with a normal final response.
serial.verification: Ran the official upstream suite for 200 passed, installed-copy tests, spec examples, distribution build, and flake8 before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required work is shown; final text notes no submit tool was available, but the current official evaluator ran and passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the same six project obligation: implement the compatibility API, project files, packaging, installability, and official tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same prompt and produced the required file tree and verification against upstream six behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference for the official task; parallel added extra raw_input/pre-commit artifacts while serial stayed closer to upstream.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation and packaging, then launched a workflow audit with 19 child logs while continuing local work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor owned implementation, packaging, verification, and final reporting without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split verification into delegated auditors but retained parent implementation ownership; serial kept all work in one local sequence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow brief told children to audit /workspace from scratch areas and report only executed findings; several verifier handoffs later debated raw_input and tooling issues.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child briefs or handoffs existed; the single actor maintained context through direct file and test checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had context transfer through audit prompts and journal results, whereas serial relied on continuous local context; no handoff gap changed the passing outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Copied upstream six files, added project files, then modified six.py to add a raw_input move and verified the expanded 201-case suite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Wrote/copy-checked six.py against upstream 1.17.0, completed supporting files, and kept the final six.py byte-identical to upstream.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main implementation path was similar, but parallel made one API-surface deviation while serial ended with upstream byte identity; both were accepted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow children returned mixed findings through the journal, but the parent had already verified the artifact and was killed near timeout after reporting auditors still running.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; local test results were consumed immediately before the final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result lifecycle was heavier and partially unfinished, but no required verifier result was needed for the accepted deliverable; serial had no delegated lifecycle risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent and child auditors operated against a shared /workspace; at least one child observed mid-audit workspace changes and re-snapshotted before continuing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: A single actor changed the workspace and then cleaned/listed the final tree, so there was no concurrent shared-state boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel exposed auditors to live workspace drift, but the observed consequence was rechecking rather than a collision, overwrite, or failed artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent verified 201 passed after adding raw_input and the completed official submit passed with evaluator ok true.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run verified byte identity, official tests, spec examples, install behavior, and official submit passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had adequate evaluator-aligned verification; parallel supplemented it with child audits while serial used local checks only.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel process reached the 2399-second timeout with returncode 143, but artifact validation and official evaluation still passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial process exited normally in about 610 seconds with remaining budget and a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed the full time window because of workflow audit breadth; this was a process-cost difference, not a task failure or retained pattern.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed cell/status.json evaluation records show both modes passed. The apparent process discrepancy is not an official outcome discordance: parallel has process_ok false because the agent hit the time limit, but artifact validation and official evaluation are ok true, while serial completed normally and also passed.
parallel_contributors: Workflow fan-out added broad audit coverage and consumed the full runtime window.
Parent continued editing shared workspace while children audited, including the raw_input addition that increased the collected official cases to 201.
serial_contributors: Single-actor implementation kept context local and finished within budget.
Serial final six.py stayed byte-identical to upstream and passed the 200-case official suite.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel added a six.moves.raw_input alias and committed test_six.py/.pre-commit-config.yaml; serial did not.
Parallel workflow children disagreed on whether raw_input/pre-commit observations were real defects; these did not affect official acceptance.
evaluator_effects: Parallel quality reports 201 passed out of total 200 because adding raw_input expanded the parameterized official tests while reward stayed 1.0.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process differences are descriptive and not retained concurrency failures

Rejected: broad workflow fan-out and timeout occurred, but no required task work was displaced before official pass.

Rejected: the executed child briefs included task, environment, scratch-dir, and reporting expectations; no omitted known requirement made child work unusable.
Rejected: children were auditing one shared implementation, not producing separately owned interoperating components with an omitted interface contract.
Rejected: no known finding is shown lost through transfer; returned journal findings remained available in workflow state.
Rejected: reports were lengthy but there is no decision-window failure or unfinished dependent action caused by unconsumed bulk.
Rejected: children observed workspace drift and re-ran checks; no stale report was consumed to create invalid verification or inconsistent integration.
Rejected: raw_input and pre-commit findings were debated, but the conflict did not remain as an unadjudicated integration blocker or failure.
Rejected: parent and evaluator acceptance rested on integrated full-suite evidence; no parent-visible end-to-end acceptance gap remained.
Rejected: verifier follow-ups used prior finding text and current workspace state, not a checkpoint-free repetition that consumed needed budget.

candidates.reason: Rejected: the process ended near timeout, but no explicit active child cancellation before needed deliverable finalization is tied to an unmet requirement.
Rejected: a usable deliverable was already in the workspace and officially evaluated; no promotable candidate failed to be placed before closure.
Rejected: after the raw_input edit the parent reran the full suite and official evaluation passed, so there was post-change verification.
Rejected: no child produced a delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve or merge; children produced audits.
Rejected: verifier results appeared in the workflow journal/state; any unfinished tail did not block a required verification step for the passing artifact.
Rejected: a child 429/unfinished audit chain did not own required implementation work, and parent testing covered delivery.
Rejected: available child results were inspected or became nonessential audits; no parent action proceeded inconsistently with a needed completed result.
Rejected: the parent actively inspected progress, ran tests, and checked the journal; timeout alone is not blind waiting.
Rejected: there were no competing cross-file designs that required unreconciled integration; parent owned the final file set.
Rejected: a child observed six.py changed under it, but there is no shown same-file edit by multiple agents requiring harmful reconciliation.
Rejected: no child-owned non-entry source was replaced by another actor in a way that lost work or provenance.
Rejected: the required deliverable was edited by the parent, not overwritten over another live deliverable owner with adverse consequence.
Rejected: final tree changes and build artifacts did not invalidate another actor final-tree output or contaminate the official artifact.
Rejected: shared workspace reads saw live parent edits, but the realized result was re-snapshotting and passing tests, not unstable-state or provenance harm.
Rejected: no child-generated fixture, cache, or temporary artifact was consumed by another actor as authoritative reference input.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The workflow timeout, child 429/unfinished audit chain, broad fan-out, and missing tail reports are one non-retained screening chain because no indispensable task work was left unmet.
Shared-workspace observations by children were considered under Same-File Collision and Unisolated Workspace Writes but suppressed because no harmful collision or provenance failure materialized.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no candidate cleared the realized adverse consequence gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Rejected timeout-only, high-fan-out, handoff-disagreement, and shared-workspace-risk near matches to avoid labeling non-material process cost.
